episode.subject_description: Door handle, the hand-operated fitting used to open and close a building door, called Türfalle in Swiss German. The target is the handle fitting itself, not the whole door, a lock mechanism, or the material from which the handle is made. It is a general type, with no particular material, design, brand, or individual handle specified.

evidence.excerpt: A door handle or doorknob is a handle used to open or close a door. Doors fitted with this handle have a latch that keeps the door shut. Pushing the handle down rotates the spindle, operating the tubular latch mechanism inside the door, allowing it to be opened.
When you turn the handle, this spindle rotates, transferring motion to the latch mechanism inside the door. With the latch bolt retracted, the door is free to swing open.

turns.question: Does it normally work by making direct physical contact with the object it controls?

evidence.excerpt: A door handle controls a door by manipulation of a latch. The latch connects the door with its frame. The handle is connected to the latch via a spindle and cylinder; when the handle is pulled or rotated, the action is carried by the spindle into the cylinder, moving the bolt and allowing the door to open or shut.

When one of the door knobs is turned, the spindle rotates along with the handle. The spindle then rotates the latch mechanism, pulling the latch bolt out of the door frame. The handle's latch assembly pulls the latch bolt in and out of the door frame.
